clues: This city grew where two rivers join to form a third, near the center of its state. It stands where rocky hills meet the flat coastal plain.
The summers here are hot and sticky, with sun that beats down hard. The winters are mild, with just a touch of cold.
On March 22, 1786, the state passed a law to build a new capital. One man's plan won, and a new town rose on the site.
This city was drawn on paper before it was built. Its planned streets came five years before the famous plan for the nation's capital city.
The governor of South Carolina works in this city. All three branches of state government sit here, beside the State House.
